Yarmouth to Freshwater

walks
Part of my Autumn and Winter Walks 2026/27.
Author

Alistair Bailey

Published

Last Updated on 2026-11-21

Saturday 21st November 2026

Visiting Dawlish almost every week for the last four years meant I got to see the sea, but my last three walks have all been inland and I needed to get back to the sea. A common misconception is that Southampton is a seaside city - not helped by the use of the marketing line Sea City - but it’s actually about 10 km inland.

Anyhow, I decided to head across the Solent to the Isle of Wight and continue walking the coastal path from Yarmouth where I left off last December when I walked from Cowes to Yarmouth.

I left home about 0800 and got the train from Southampton Central to Lymington Pier to catch the 1000 ferry to Yarmouth. It was pretty chilly, but dry and sunny and the Solent was flat as a millpond. I’ve been very lucky with the weather so far this autumn.

I’m usually pretty self-sufficient for food and drink, but in a nod to the “use it or lose it” theory about having nice things, I’m trying to make a point of spending at least a little money wherever I go. Not in a do-gooding hair shirt way, but if I see something nice, then it’s nice to support it. This time it was PO41 coffee shop (Figure 7) where I got a decent coffee and a bit of caramel apple cake. The cake I ate whilst waiting for the ferry back as the sun was starting to set. The coffee and cake cost £8. I have a speciality coffee subscription that costs me about £0.70 a cup of top quality coffee, and I can buy a pastry from Lidl for £1. It’s quite a differential, and whilst I can afford it, I am torn between the fact I can make/buy/bring something just as nice and wanting to live in a world with nice things and people to have employment, even if it’s a stepping stone job and my personal contribution is very small.

The route I plotted follows the coastal path, but as anyone who’s walked the IoW coastal path knows, there’s a lot of erosion and landslips - the joke being that in 10 years it’ll be the Isle of W - and so re-routing is common (Figure 27), and the other common gripe is that much of the path is more coast-adjacent than actually on the coast. But this was a nicer stretch than Cowes to Yarmouth, although I didn’t see any red squirrels this time.

I started walking at about 1040. The route starts off pretty gentle for the first hour or so, with a view back to Hurst Castle from near Fort Albert. But once one gets out of Totland Bay, it is very up and down and by lunchtime I was pretty hot. I stopped on a bench overlooking the Needles before going down and back up past Alum Bay, around the Needles and down and back up to the Tennyson Monument, and then the final descent to Freshwater Bay. I walked up to the bus stop at School Green Road by Stroud Recreation Ground to get the number 7 bus back to Yarmouth at 1511. It’s about an hour extra walking to follow the Freshwater Way to Yarmouth instead.

I got the 1605 ferry back to Lymington and got home at 1800. The plotted route was 17.5 km, but I walked closer to 21 km.
